title: A study map with self-testing
description: Hide a branch, recall what was in it and check against your own notes.

blocks.text: In the reviews students describe maps as a way to work through and remember material. A self-testing mode on your own notes can be developed out of that: close a branch and try to reconstruct what was in it. The need for a map is borne out by examples, while the benefit of this particular mode still needs testing.

quote.text: just started doing mind maps as a form of active reading and i ACED my very first ever quiz because i remembered its placement in the mind map i made. For a broke medical student, i can’t afford other fancy mind-map-making sites

blocks.text: Add temporary hiding of branches, questions attached to nodes and marks on the difficult spots. Use the same notes without creating a separate copy.
Do not treat revealing the answer as proof of knowledge. The user needs a choice about what to revise next and a way to correct a mistake in the original material.
